newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds unchanged as trade picks up.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds unchanged as trade picks up.

text.p: Irish bonds were broadly unchanged on Thursday amid steadier trade as the market overcame worries triggered by reports of recent central bank intervention on the interbank market, dealers said.

"There was confusion yesterday about what looked like a central bank move to tighten rates," a dealer said. "Today the market seems to have recognised that they (the central bank) are just panel beating and that it's not a policy thing."
The market had seen steady short-end action since early in the session, the dealer said.

The short end of the curve was affected on Wednesday by a slight tightening of interbank market rates as the central bank was reported to have bought up Irish pounds, ostensibly to bolster the punt against sterling.
"Because it was a quiet day yesterday the effect was a little out of proportion - that's been rectified," the dealer added.

Dealers said there had been a steepening of the curve on Thursday, with Irish bonds yielding 143 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area - a narrowing of four basis points - and 89 basis points over bunds in the 10-year, a narrowing of one basis point.

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up five pence from Wednesday's close at 101.92 to yield 5.99 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 fell 10 pence to 108.40 to yield 6.74 percent.
Dealers said that the near term focus of the Irish market would be the French rather than the British election.
"Really the only game in town is EMU - we know where we stand and we're watching the other players to see whether they will be ready on time," a dealer said.

"If it looks likely that the current French government will be re-elected with a fresh mandate to pursue a restrictive fiscal policy in order to meet the (EU) criteria, then that will be positive for the Irish market."
